name: Baihu #70 — Phoenix of Western Steel and Retribution
title: Phoenix of Western Steel and Retribution
description:
Ancient Chinese chronicles speak of Baihu, the divine guardian of the West, embodiment of steel, disciplined warfare, and rightful retribution. His arrival once signaled the downfall of cities ruled by pride, corruption, and unmeasured force. Temples devoted to him were adorned with narrow metal banners and tiger-etched ritual patterns, and his priests conducted rites under the dry western winds, when justice required a blade rather than a plea. To mortals, Baihu was a boundary: the moment where arrogance met consequence.

When the celestial beasts vanished from mortal sight, Baihu’s spirit did not fade. Instead, it was reborn through the burning cycle of the Phoenix, feathers banded with tiger stripes and veined with metallic luminescence. His wings now carry the heat of purification, and his curved blades enforce the old law of balance. He rises only when evil believes itself untouchable, striking in a single, perfect motion. Thus, the Phoenix Baihu stands as the searing judgment of the West—unseen until the instant everything ends.
